title: Injectivity and projective cokernel descend from a principal cover
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, M a finitely generated R-module and N a finitely presented R-module. Let f : M -> N be R-linear. Suppose that for each prime ideal p of R there exists s outside p such that the map R_s tensor_R M -> R_s tensor_R N induced by f is injective and its cokernel is projective over R_s. Then f is injective and N / image(f) is projective over R. No flatness or projectivity of M or N is assumed.

source.place: Algebra, Section 10.23 (Tag 00EN), Lemma 10.23.1 (1),(4); Lemma 10.39.18 (Tag 00HT) (2),(5); Lemma 10.78.2 (Tag 00NX) (1) implies (2)

proof.text: Let S be the set of elements for which the localized map is injective. If its span were proper, a maximal ideal containing it would contradict the given prime-cover hypothesis. Apply Mathlib Module.eq_of_isLocalized_span to the maps x ↦ 1 tensor x: equality of f x and f y implies equality of their local images by localized injectivity. Therefore f is injective.

The quotient Q=N/range f is finitely presented by Module.finitePresentation_of_surjective and Submodule.fg_range. Let S be the set where the localized cokernel is projective; its span is the unit ideal by the same maximal-ideal argument. Each localized cokernel is flat over the localization and hence over R by Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization. Tensor right exactness (lTensor.equiv), together with Submodule.Quotient.restrictScalarsEquiv and the equality of the restricted base-change range with the lTensor range, identifies this cokernel as an R-module with the tensor localization of Q. Transfer flatness along this equivalence, descend with Module.flat_of_isLocalized_span, and conclude projectivity with Module.Flat.projective_of_finitePresentation.

lean.statement:
theorem injective_projective_cokernel_of_principal_cover
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R]
    {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] [Module.Finite R M]
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module.FinitePresentation R N]
    (f : M →ₗ[R] N)
    (h : ∀ (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime], ∃ s : R, s ∉ p ∧
      Function.Injective (f.baseChange (Localization.Away s)) ∧
      Module.Projective (Localization.Away s)
        (TensorProduct R (Localization.Away s) N ⧸
          LinearMap.range (f.baseChange (Localization.Away s)))) :
    Function.Injective f ∧ Module.Projective R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range f)
